A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B. Their material supports a reliable comparison, including relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression, image-classification, language-understanding, uncertainty, sensitivity, and runtime experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and runtime results and presents revised image-sensitivity examples.

M1.justification: The prediction algorithm, Gaussian propagation, local linearisation, and transformer/KFAC handling remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 removes the optional sensitivity formulation that learns a covariance shared by each digit class, including v1 Eq. (89), while retaining per-image sensitivity optimisation.

E1.justification: The UCI, MNIST-like, vision-transformer, language-understanding, and OOD datasets and tasks are retained. Changes to covariance sharing and optimisation occur within the existing MNIST sensitivity task, without changing its data or population coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same sampling, GLM, moment-matching, MAP, and last-layer Laplace comparators. Removing the class-shared sensitivity experiment does not introduce or replace a comparator in the retained experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 changes the stated initial input covariance from 0.1 to 1e-5 and the stopping tolerance from 0.1 to 0.01. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Section 4.3 still specifies 0.1, creating a discrepancy.

E4.justification: v2 removes the class-shared covariance sensitivity analysis and its figure, while revising the individual-image examples. The OOD tests, sampling-budget analysis, local-linearity analysis, transformer covariance comparison, and runtime analyses remain.

E5.justification: The statistical reporting practices are retained: five-fold regression evaluation, standard errors, paired t-tests at p = 0.05, and runtime means and standard deviations from ten measurements with the first discarded. No changed seed or repetition policy is reported.

E6.justification: Figures 5 and 10 show different sensitivity examples, and Appendix B.3 changes the reported typical optimisation length from approximately 900 to 700 iterations under revised settings. The class-shared finding of similar MAP and Bayesian sensitivities is removed. Benchmark and runtime table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Most mathematical material is retained. Appendix A.4 drops the trailing D from C[...]D in the covariance-extraction sentence, although the preceding reconstruction expression still includes it, introducing a limited mathematical inconsistency. The class-shared sensitivity objective in v1 Eq. (89) is also removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: sampling-free prediction through local approximations, support for different architectures and covariance structures, and applications to uncertainty and sensitivity analysis. Wording changes do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: The substantive interpretations and limitations are retained. Explicit residual-independence wording in Section 3.2 repeats a qualification already present in v1's limitations; the added low-overhead wording summarises the existing runtime discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds an open-source library pointer beneath the abstract and explicitly states that sensitivity optimisation is performed independently for each image. Appendix B.3 also revises the documented covariance, tolerance, and typical iteration count; other implementation and hardware information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Baumann et al. (2024), Post-hoc probabilistic vision-language models, as another application of post-hoc Bayesian methods. The broader related-work coverage and positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes distributed grammar, spelling, and terminology corrections, adds an introductory roadmap to Appendix B, and changes the publication header. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Sensitivity illustrations in Figures 1, 5, and 10 receive new digit examples and colouring. The per-class sensitivity figure is removed, and v1 Figures 12–15 become v2 Figures 11–14. Several retained figures and tables move, without a substantial redesign of the document.

improvement.justification: v2 improves prose and provides a useful code-access pointer, but removes supplementary sensitivity evidence and introduces a disagreement between Section 4.3's stopping threshold of 0.1 and Appendix B.3's 0.01. The main empirical evidence is unchanged, and the revised sensitivity settings are not justified against the earlier settings. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
